ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure shows a circular sector and its interior, with a right-angle quarter-circle region missing at the lower right, so what remains is a three-quarter circular sector. The two straight sides in the figure are radii, of which the horizontal radius is labeled 4, indicating that the radius of the circle in which this sector lies is 4 inches; the gap corresponding between the two radii is 90°, and the retained arc is 270°. Reasoning: When this sector is rolled into a cone, the sector radius becomes the slant height of the cone, so the cone slant height l=4. The arc length of the sector becomes the circumference of the base circle of the cone. The arc length of the three-quarter circle is (3/4)(2π·4)=6π. Let the radius of the cone base be r, then 2πr=6π, so r=3. The height h of the cone, base radius 3, and slant height 4 form a right triangle, therefore h^2+3^2=4^2, giving h^2=7, h=√7. The cone volume V=(1/3)πr^2h=(1/3)π·9·√7=3π√7.

raw_record.question_text: A three-quarter sector of a circle of radius $4$ inches together with its interior can be rolled up to form the lateral surface area of a right circular cone by taping together along the two radii shown. What is the volume of the cone in cubic inches?

method.method_draft: First read the image as a three-quarter circular sector: the two straight edges are radii meeting at a right angle gap, and the horizontal radius is labeled 4, so the sector radius is 4 and the remaining arc is 270 degrees. From the text, the sector is rolled into a right circular cone by taping the two radii together. Use the net relationship that the sector radius becomes the cone slant height, and the sector arc length becomes the circumference of the cone base. Compute arc length as (3/4)(2π·4)=6π, so 2πr=6π gives base radius r=3. Then use the right triangle formed by cone height, base radius, and slant height: h^2+3^2=4^2, so h=√7. Finally apply V=(1/3)πr^2h=(1/3)π·9·√7=3π√7.

From the text, this entire sector becomes exactly the lateral surface area of the cone. Compute the sector area directly: (3/4)π(4^2)=12π.
